chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hukam narrated to us, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Razqi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them all).

He said: Indeed, Paradise has eight gates. One gate is for the Prophets and the Truthful ones. One gate is for the Martyrs and the Righteous ones. Five gates are for our Shiites and our beloved ones. I will remain standing at the Bridge (al-Sirat), supplicating and saying: 'O Lord, grant peace to my followers, my beloved, and my supporters, and whoever acknowledged my authority in this world.' Then the call will come from beneath the Throne, 'Your supplication has been answered and intercession has been granted for your followers.' And every man from my followers, and whoever acknowledged my authority, helped me, and fought whoever fought me, by deed or by word, will intercede for seventy thousand of his neighbors and relatives. And the last gate is for the rest of the Muslims, from those who testified that there is no god but Allah, and there was not in their hearts the weight of a speck of dust of hatred for us, the People of the House.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the eight gates of Paradise according to the Shiites of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* elaborates on the eschatological hierarchy of Paradise, emphasizing the unique status of the *Shi'a* (followers) of the Ahl al-Bayt who occupy five of the eight gates. It underscores the concept of *Shafa'ah* (intercession), where the Imams and their devoted followers secure salvation not only for themselves but also for a vast number of their kin and supporters, while a distinct gate remains for other Muslims who maintain love for the Ahl al-Bayt without harboring hatred in their hearts.
